items.title: Harvil1/codeAgent
items.excerpt: CodeAgent is an open-source coding agent that lives in your terminal. It understands your repository, plans multi-step changes, writes and edits files, runs commands and tests, and iterates until the task is done — all with a transparent, extensible tool loop.
items.summary: CodeAgent is an open-source coding agent running in terminal that understands repositories, plans multi-step changes, writes and edits files, runs commands and tests, iterating until task completion with transparent tool loop.
items.usefulness: Could support learning to build Python tools by providing a working reference implementation of agent planning, file manipulation, and command execution workflows in a contained environment.
items.to_verify: Whether CodeAgent's tool loop implementation handles Python-specific patterns; how it manages state across multi-step repository changes; actual error recovery mechanics.

items.title: Using LLM for confidence scoring is a bad idea
items.summary: HN discussion claims using LLM for confidence scoring is problematic, authored as blog post exploring this limitation.
items.usefulness: Could inform governance decisions about LLM reliability assessment in Python applications where confidence scores drive downstream actions or safety-critical logic.
items.to_verify: Specific failure modes when LLMs provide confidence scores; whether proposed alternative exists; empirical evidence distinguishing this from general LLM calibration issues.
